transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Anika Bose (Nimbus - Head of MLOps), Marcus Li (Nimbus - CTO), Priya Singh (Nimbus - Procurement)

Summary: Quick renewal + expansion check-in to confirm capacity needs for Q2, discuss adding two additional regions (eu-west & ap-south), and align on contract extension timeline. Action items and next steps captured at end.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Quick check is this still a good time?
[00:08] Anika: Yeah, perfect. Thanks Maya. We got Marcus and Priya on as well, just to make sure procurement and infra alignment happen.
[00:15] Marcus: Hi all, sorry for joining a couple minutes late, jump in.
[00:20] Maya: No worries. So agenda, real quick: renewal timing, capacity increase for Dedicated pools, multi-region add-on (EU + APAC), and any contract/legal asks. Carlos will cover the perf/benchmark ask.
[00:32] Carlos: Hey all, I'll keep it technical and brief. From what we saw on your production metrics last quarter, peak concurrent streams hit about 350 at 95th percentile, with median seq length around 512 tokens for generation flows. That maps to roughly X p100H100 slots I'll confirm exact number after we run the benchmark.
[00:50] Anika: Right, we had a spike around holiday traffic and we want buffer for growth, planning for 2x baseline. Also on latency we saw 180-220ms p50 which is fine for batch features but for real-time chat we need to get p50 under 120 if possible.
[01:10] Carlos: Understood options are: increase Dedicated capacity, enable more aggressive batching and KV cache tuning, or add a lower-latency region closer to users. Tradeoffs: capacity reduces queuing but increases cost; region add lowers network latency but adds egress/replication considerations.
[01:30] Priya: From procurement side we need to understand cost delta. If you can send a clean line item for Dedicated + multi-region that helps our SOW. Also any changes to billing cadence  annual vs quarterly.
[01:45] Maya: Absolutely, we'll put together a refreshed quote. For multi-region we typically recommend replicating critical model variants only, not full catalog, to save costs. I can include both full-replication and partial-replication options.
[01:59] Marcus: Also want to confirm security posture  we need KMS integration and audit logs for the additional region. Our security team insists on HSM-backed keys for production.
[02:12] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll include the integration steps and any latency impact notes in the security doc.
[02:24] Anika: On the benchmark  Carlos, can you walk through what you'll need from us and how long it will take?
[02:30] Carlos: Sure. Ideally a sample workload: prompt set, request distribution, and a staging endpoint that mirrors the payloads. We'll run a 2-hour benchmark across candidate instance sizes and quantization profiles. Expect initial results within 48 hours of data receipt.
[02:46] Anika: I can pull the prompt set and a synthetic traffic profile today, will share by EOD.
[02:50] Carlos: Great. That will let us size Dedicated GPU pools and recommend the autoscale headroom.

[03:05] Speaker 1: (minor crosstalk)

[03:10] Priya: On contract extension, are we looking at a 12 or 24 month term? Does longer term get a discount?
[03:18] Maya: Yes, standard is 12 months but we offer stepped discounts for 24-month commitments, and a further discount if you commit to reserved capacity levels. I'll include tabled options in the quote.
[03:32] Marcus: We're leaning toward 24 months if the price and capacity guarantees align. We need predictable unit economics.
[03:38] Anika: Also, on the dedicated pools can Redwood guarantee capacity during model upgrades and rollouts? We run canary and A/B traffic.
[03:48] Carlos: Good question. We support canary rollouts and route-splitting. For guaranteed capacity during rollouts we recommend reserved pool + buffer headroom. We can config automatic fallback to hosted model variants if a node goes down to preserve availability.
[04:05] Anika: That fallback sounds useful, though we need to be careful about data residency and whether requests hit hosted endpoints.
[04:12] Maya: For Private/VPC deployments, fallback stays within your VPC if you choose that option. For Dedicated we can keep traffic in specified regions only. We'll call that in the notes.
[04:26] Priya: Can you confirm audit logs retention? Our compliance needs 1 year of fine-grained logs.
[04:33] Maya: Redwood offers configurable retention; standard is 90 days but enterprise packages go to 12 months or custom retention with extra storage fees. I'll put retention tiers in the doc.
[04:46] Marcus: On multi-region replication  how does model state sync work? Is KV cache synced or is it per-region?
[04:54] Carlos: KV cache is per-region by default; we replicate model binaries and weights. For low-latency use cases we recommend per-region warm-up with periodic weight syncs; KV cache warm-up happens organically as traffic comes in. There's an option for pre-warming via synthetic traffic which we can run as part of the benchmark.
[05:12] Anika: Pre-warm sounds good. We can provide synthetic traces.

[05:20] Maya: Any blockers from legal or procurement right now?
[05:23] Priya: We need Redwood's standard MSA and also confirmation on data processing addendum for GDPR since we'll have EU region traffic. Also need SOC 2 Type II and penetration test summary.
[05:34] Maya: We'll attach SOC 2 and penetration summary. The DPA template is standard; legal can redline. I'll include the MSA and a suggested redline window.
[05:45] Marcus: A quick note on cost  our finance team is sensitive to variable per-token spend. If we commit to reserved throughput, can we get predictable per-token equivalent?
[05:55] Maya: Yes, reserved capacity converts to a predictable per-token cost (roughly average based on expected utilization). We'll show scenarios: low-utilization (worse unit cost) vs high-utilization (best unit cost).
[06:09] Anika: On metrics  can Redwood present token-level cost breakdown by route? That was super useful last time.
[06:15] Carlos: Yep, Console shows per-route/per-model latency and token cost. We can share a dashboard snapshot in the follow-up.

[06:26] Maya: Ok let's talk timeline  you mentioned wanting to finalize before end of month?
[06:30] Priya: Procurement needs contract signed by Feb 10 to align with fiscal planning. So ideally we have pricing and legal in the next two weeks.
[06:39] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get the quote and contract template within five business days.

[06:45] Marcus: One more technical ask  we run a private deployment in our VPC for sensitive models right now, but we'd like Redwood Dedicated for public-facing features. Can we have hybrid routing so sensitive requests stay in VPC and others hit Dedicated?
[07:00] Carlos: Yes, smart routing policies support that. You can route by tag, route, or model version. We can set automatic fallbacks and priority routing to ensure sensitive traffic never leaves the VPC.
[07:12] Anika: Great. That solves a lot of compliance worries.

[07:20] Maya: I'll recap next steps at the end. Any other open questions?
[07:25] Priya: On invoicing, do you accept purchase orders and Net30?
[07:29] Maya: Yes, standard Net30 with PO is fine; larger contracts can get Net45 with credit approval. We'll note that.

[07:35] Carlos: Quick follow-up on benchmarking  we'll test quantized variants as well to show cost/latency tradeoffs. If you have a preference for INT8 vs FP16 let us know but we'll include both.
[07:47] Anika: Include both, and highlight any quality diffs if you see regressions.

[07:55] Maya: OK, to recap:
- Maya will send revised pricing with dedicated capacity options, multi-region partial/full replication, and term options (12 vs 24mo)
- Carlos will run a 2-hour benchmark once Anika provides prompt set and traffic profile; results to be uploaded
- Redwood to attach SOC2, pen test summary, DPA and KMS/HSM integration notes
- Priya to confirm PO/billing details and timeline (aiming for contract by Feb 10)

[08:25] Marcus: That covers it from our side. Thanks, team.
[08:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the quote and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[08:36] Anika: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
